newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Steel says no merger on near horizon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Steel says no merger on near horizon.

text.p: Despite recent speculation that USX Corp's U.S. Steel unit may soon merge with a competitor or combine its operations with those of one, the nation's largest steelmaker will likely stand on its own for a while, the chairman of USX said Monday.

"I would say the probability of doing something in the near future is very small," Tom Usher told Reuters in a brief interview. "We're not talking with anybody. I think the opportunities (for steelmakers) to do things like this were probably better in the past, when there were a lot of operational synergies (between companies.) Usher was in New York to announce a $100 million advertising campaign that will be launched later this month by the Steel Alliance, a consortium of U.S. steelmakers.

"I think what Mr. Wilhelm was trying to say is we continue to look at opportunities and we're certainly doing whatever we can to improve shareholder value. If that would include some kind of alliance, either full or in part with another company, we're always aware of those things. But yet it would be a difficult thing to do," Usher said.

Several industry analysts have also said U.S. steelmakers need to consolidate to reduce the number of players who supply large-volume buyers, including auto and appliance makers. That would allow prices to rise, some analysts have said.

Usher voiced skepticism of that viewpoint. "I'm not sure that any combination of two companies could have any significant impact on price," he said. "The idea that major consolidation would allow pricing to get up...(increase) I don't think that would be correct."
Usher said prices paid by large-volume buyers are more driven by market strength, rather than too many steel suppliers competing against one another for business.

"Prices in automotive and any other industry have gone up and down and a lot of it is dependent on market strength," he said. "A couple years ago, there were increases (in vehicle builds) and it was a tight market for steel. Prices (went up.) But it was driven by the market as opposed to steel companies competing against each other."

Separately, Usher said he expects a strong steel market this year. "We see nothing that indicates the market weakening. Every consumer segment we sell to is strong. Automotive is strong, appliance is strong, construction is strong...we see a strong market."
Commenting on second quarter earnings projections, Usher said, "There's nothing that has come out of the analysts' expectations that causes me any great alarm."
Wall Street's consensus estimate for the second quarter is $1.10 per share, based on 12 estimates ranging from $0.82 to $1.40, according to First Call.

The consensus for the full year is $3.76 per share. "I'm very comfortable that absent some unforeseen thing, if the year turns out as we think it will, that seems like a number that is certainly do-able," Usher said.
